id: title:TueHaulund:expose products enable so agents can turn products on

review.posthog_relevance: Adds a new MCP tool and permission scope to the PostHog API, potentially enabling AI agents to programmatically request product activation.
review.reason: Adds a new MCP tool named 'products-enable' with its handler, OpenAPI definition, and Zod schemas, alongside a required permission scope. This represents a substantive, bounded capability improvement by extending the PostHog API with a new programmable interface for external agents, rather than a narrow maintenance or documentation-only change.
review.uncertainty: The actual adoption and operational benefit of this MCP integration are not demonstrated by the code alone; the implementation could remain unused. No production incident or severe systemic risk is evidenced, and the tier is not raised to 3 without broader systemic impact or critical path dependency.

observations.limitations: This chunk represents a single, cohesive change group. No unrelated PRs detected. No tier assignment performed.

observations.behavior: Adds a new MCP tool named 'products-enable' to the PostHog API, including its OpenAPI definition, Zod request/response schemas, handler implementation, and registration.
observations.posthog_connection: Adds a new tool to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface, allowing external agents to request enabling of PostHog products. This could allow AI agents to programmatically activate session replay, error tracking, or conversations for a project, potentially automating setup or diagnostics. The implementation includes the tool definition, request parameters, and the actual API-to

observations.behavior: Adds the 'product_enablement:write' scope to the list of required scopes for the new tool.
observations.posthog_connection: Associates the new tool with a specific permission scope, establishing the authorization boundary for this capability. This could allow PostHog to enforce access control, ensuring only authenticated users or roles with this permission can invoke the tool.

observations.behavior: Adds the tool definition to the generated OpenAPI specification, including metadata and annotations.
